The Polished standard

No “looks good from the doorway.”

Every vacant turn is scoped before work starts, cleaned room by room, and checked against the same finish list.

  • ✓
    Inside the empty spacesCabinets, drawers, closets, microwave, and reachable shelving.
  • ✓
    Edges and touchpointsBaseboards, door frames, switches, handles, sills, and fixtures.
  • ✓
    Kitchen and bath resetCountertops, sinks, stovetop, shower, tub, toilet, and appliance fronts.
  • ✓
    Floors finished lastVacuumed or swept, then mopped after the rest of the clean is complete.

Straight answers

Before you hand over the keys.

Vacant or near-empty is the standard. A few remaining items can be discussed in the scope, but packing, hauling, and junk removal are not part of a normal turn clean.
The core scope covers floors, reachable surfaces, cabinet and drawer interiors, closets, baseboards, fixtures, appliance fronts, bathrooms, and the inside of the microwave. Oven and refrigerator interiors can be added.
Yes. The service is structured around vacant turns: one point of contact, a repeatable scope, access instructions, deadline, and finish documentation.
Heavy buildup, excessive pet hair, debris, occupied rooms, exterior glass, and specialty surfaces can change the time or require a separate quote. Flagging those details early keeps the handoff clean.

Less downtime. Fewer loose ends.
